extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials and staff responsible for preparing, submitting, and coordinating documents for publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER and related Office of the Federal Register publications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and content rules for preparing, transmitting, scheduling, and distributing documents for publication and public inspection in the FEDERAL REGISTER, Code of Federal Regulations, and related publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel lists of United States Code citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical lists of all sections of the current edition of the United States Code which are cited by issuing agencies as rulemaking authority for currently effective regulations in the Code of Federal Regulations; arranged in the order of the titles and sections of the United States Code with parallel citations to the pertinent titles and parts of the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Located in the Code of Federal Regulations Index or at such other place as the Director of the Federal Register considers appropriate; lists shall be arranged in title/section order and provide parallel citations to enable users to find precise text in effect on a given date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel tables of Presidential documents and agency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables of proclamations, Executive orders, and similar Presidential documents which are cited as rulemaking authority in currently effective regulations in the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published in the Code of Federal Regulations Index or at such other place as the Director considers appropriate to show connections between Presidential documents and agency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of CFR sections affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the text of each Code of Federal Regulations volume, a numerical list of sections which are affected by documents published in the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listings shall refer to FEDERAL REGISTER pages and be designed to enable the user of the Code to find the precise text that was in effect on a given date in the period covered; historical multi-year lists exist (e.g., 1949–1963, 1964–1972, 1973–1985).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of publication (authorized formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code of Federal Regulations may be published in paper, microfiche, and online formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director of the Federal Register may regulate format according to user needs and GPO compatibility, provide for separate bound books as necessary, set requirements for microfiche images, and oversee organization and access for the online edition (GPO Access, 44 U.S.C. 4101).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cooperation with publication deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall cooperate in keeping publication of the Code current by complying promptly with deadlines set by the Director of the Federal Register and the Public Printer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are expected to meet deadlines to ensure timely publication and currency of the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of citation for the CFR
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code of Federal Regulations may be cited by title and section; the short form 'CFR' may be used for 'Code of Federal Regulations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: '1 CFR 10.2' refers to title 1, Code of Federal Regulations, part 10, section 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement for The United States Government Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register shall separately publish annually or at times designated by the Administrative Committee a special edition called 'The United States Government Manual' (or other title the Committee considers appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may issue special supplements to the Manual when such supplementation is considered in the public interest (authority: 44 U.S.C. 1506).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and required content of the Government Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual shall contain appropriate information about the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches; for major Executive agencies it shall include descriptions of the agency's public purposes, programs and functions; established places and methods for the public to obtain information and make submittals or requests; and lists of officials heading major operating units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May also include brief quasi-official or supplemental information that the Director considers of enough public interest to warrant inclusion; formal executive documents promulgated in accordance with law also included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format, indexing, and ancillaries for Presidential publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents and the annual Public Papers of the Presidents shall be published in paper and online editions, appropriately indexed, and contain ancillary information on Presidential activities and documents not carried in full text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admin. Committee publishes in binding and style suitable for public and official use; online editions available on GPO Access (44 U.S.C. 4101); annual Public Papers cover calendar years, divided into books as needed, and include additional illustrative material respecting significant Presidential documents and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription availability and pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Government Printing Office produces paper and microfiche editions and the Superintendent of Documents makes them available for sale to the public; fees are payable in advance and publications are not available for free distribution to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific subscription prices and options are listed (e.g., daily FEDERAL REGISTER paper edition $699/year; combined subscriptions, microfiche rates, single-issue prices); online editions available via GPO Access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official distribution within the Federal Government
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the FEDERAL REGISTER, Code of Federal Regulations, Government Manual, Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents, and Public Papers of the Presidents shall be made available without charge to specified congressional, judicial, and executive recipients, based on written requests and prescribed quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Members of Congress provided specified numbers of copies (e.g., up to five daily FR copies), congressional committees provided numbers needed for official use upon written request, Supreme Court and other courts provided needed copies, executive agencies provided needed copies (with limits such as not to exceed 300 copies of individual CFR titles per agency). Procedures exist for requisitions, overruns, advance printing and binding requisitions (Standard Form 1), and ordering extra copies at cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services to agencies: assistance and information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall assist agencies in complying with publication laws to assure efficient public service in promulgating administrative documents having the effect of legal notice or of law, including answering inquiries in person, by telephone, or in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office staff provide informal assistance/advice on regulatory drafting, procedures, promulgation practices; reproduction or certified copies of original acts and documents furnished at cost; Director may prepare and distribute information/instructions and develop technical instruction programs to promote effective compliance (see §§ 15.1–15.4, 15.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of agency representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall designate from its officers or employees a liaison officer and alternate, a certifying officer and alternate, and an authorizing officer and alternate; same person may serve multiple roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must notify the Director of names, titles, addresses, telephone numbers of designees and promptly notify of changes; liaison should be directly involved in the agency's regulatory program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison officer duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent the agency in all matters relating to submission of documents to the Office of the Federal Register and general compliance; be responsible for effective distribution and use within the agency of Federal Register drafting/publication information; promote agency participation in technical instruction; be available to discuss documents submitted for publication with editors of the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These duties are set out in § 16.2 and liaison selection should consider these responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifying officer duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for attaching the required number of true copies of each original document submitted by the agency and for making the certification required by §§ 18.5 and 18.6 of the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures submission includes proper certified copies and certifications for Office of the Federal Register processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorizing officer duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for furnishing to the Director a current mailing list of officers or employees of the agency who are authorized to receive the FEDERAL REGISTER, the Code of Federal Regulations, and the Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents for official use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeps Director informed of authorized recipients within the agency for official distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt and processing hours and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of the Federal Register receives documents only during official working hours unless special arrangements are made; upon receipt each document shall be held for confidential processing until it is filed for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should plan submissions according to working hours and confidentiality handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular schedule procedure and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents received that meet requirements and are received by 2:00 p.m. shall be assigned to the regular schedule; receipt by 2:00 p.m. is considered a request for filing for public inspection and publication on the regular schedule unless special arrangements or deferred schedule applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents received after 2:00 p.m. that meet requirements are assigned to the next working day's regular schedule; the regular schedule maps receipt day to file-for-inspection and publication days (e.g., received Monday before 2:00 p.m.: filed Wednesday, published Thursday), with adjustments for federal holidays; notices under the Government in the Sunshine Act are placed on immediate public inspection after processing and assigned publication dates based on 4:00 p.m. receipt rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and procedure for emergency publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency schedule is designed for fastest possible publication of documents involving prevention, alleviation, control, or relief of an emergency situation; an agency requesting emergency publication shall briefly describe the emergency and benefits to immediate publication in a letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director shall assign a document to the emergency schedule when the Director concurs and it is feasible; such documents shall be published as soon as possible and filed for public inspection the working day before publication unless emergency filing for public inspection is also requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and procedure for emergency filing for public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may request emergency filing for public inspection to provide the fastest possible public access after processing and scheduling; emergency filing is a special arrangement that deviates from the regular schedule and keeps the document on public inspection until published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be made by letter briefly describing the emergency and benefits to immediate public access; Director approves emergency filing when the Director concurs and it is feasible; approved documents shall be filed as soon as possible after processing and scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for deferred schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: A document may be assigned to the deferred schedule if there are technical problems, unusual or lengthy tables or illustrations, or the document's size requires extraordinary processing time, or if the agency requests a deferred publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of the Federal Register staff will notify the agency if its documents must be assigned to a deferred schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originals and copies required for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided for Executive orders and proclamations, each agency submitting a document to be filed and published shall send an original and two duplicate originals or certified copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the document is printed or processed on both sides, one of the copies sent must be a collated, single-sided copy (see § 18.1); follow exceptions in § 19.2 for Executive orders and proclamations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on combined category documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will not accept a document for filing and publication if it combines material that must appear under more than one category in the FEDERAL REGISTER (e.g., a document may not contain both rulemaking and notice of proposed rulemaking material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where two related documents are to be published in the same FEDERAL REGISTER issue, the agency may insert a cross-reference in each document to connect them.
